body.title: At the Coffee Shop
body.script:
Anna: Hi! Can I have a small coffee, please?
Waiter: Sure. Anything to eat?
Anna: Yes, one chocolate cake, please.
Waiter: OK. That's four dollars, please.
Anna: Here you are. Oh, and can I sit near the window?
Waiter: Yes, of course. Table five is free.
Anna: Thank you! Oh no, I don't have my phone. Can I use your phone? I want to call my friend Ben.
Waiter: No problem. Here you are.
Anna: Thanks. Ben is at the bus stop. He is coming in ten minutes.

questions.prompt: What does Anna want to drink?

explanation.explanation_en: Anna says, 'Can I have a small coffee, please?'
explanation.explanation_vi: Anna nói: 'Can I have a small coffee, please?' (Cho tôi một cà phê nhỏ).

questions.prompt: What does Anna want to eat?

explanation.explanation_en: Anna asks for 'one chocolate cake, please.'
explanation.explanation_vi: Anna yêu cầu 'one chocolate cake' (một chiếc bánh sô-cô-la).

explanation.explanation_en: The waiter says, 'That's four dollars, please.'
explanation.explanation_vi: Nhân viên nói: 'That's four dollars, please.' (Bốn đô la).

explanation.explanation_en: Anna says, 'Ben is at the bus stop.'
explanation.explanation_vi: Anna nói: 'Ben is at the bus stop.' (Ben đang ở trạm xe buýt).

explanation.explanation_en: Anna says, 'He is coming in ten minutes.'
explanation.explanation_vi: Anna nói: 'He is coming in ten minutes.' (Anh ấy sẽ đến trong mười phút).

Questions and options are single words or short phrases, matching A1 listening comprehension descriptors.

body.title: Listening Basics - Store Announcement
body.prompt: Listen to the announcement: 'Good afternoon, shoppers. The supermarket will close at nine o'clock tonight. Please finish your shopping before that time. Thank you.' What time does the supermarket close?
body.script: Good afternoon, shoppers. The supermarket will close at nine o'clock tonight. Please finish your shopping before that time. Thank you.
body.transcript: Good afternoon, shoppers. The supermarket will close at nine o'clock tonight. Please finish your shopping before that time. Thank you.

_provenance.cefr_reasoning: The item uses very simple present-tense sentences, common everyday vocabulary (supermarket, close, shopping), and a short announcement asking for a single time detail. This matches A1 listening comprehension of basic phrases and common expressions.

explanation.explanation_en: In listening comprehension, listen for key details like times and numbers. The announcement clearly says the supermarket closes 'at nine o'clock tonight'.
explanation.explanation_vi: Trong nghe hiểu, cần chú ý các chi tiết quan trọng như thời gian và con số. Thông báo nói rõ siêu thị đóng cửa 'vào lúc chín giờ tối nay'.

body.title: At the Coffee Shop
body.prompt: Listen to the conversation at the coffee shop. What does Anna want in her coffee?
body.script: Anna: Good morning! Can I have a small coffee, please? Waiter: Sure. Would you like milk or sugar? Anna: Just milk, please. No sugar. Waiter: OK. Anything to eat? Anna: Yes, one piece of chocolate cake, please. Waiter: That's four dollars, please. Anna: Here you are. Thank you!
body.transcript: Anna: Good morning! Can I have a small coffee, please? Waiter: Sure. Would you like milk or sugar? Anna: Just milk, please. No sugar. Waiter: OK. Anything to eat? Anna: Yes, one piece of chocolate cake, please. Waiter: That's four dollars, please. Anna: Here you are. Thank you!

_provenance.cefr_reasoning: The item uses very common vocabulary (milk, sugar, coffee, please) and simple present comprehension of a short everyday phrase ('Just milk, please. No sugar.'). Options are single basic words/phrases, matching A1 everyday expressions.

explanation.explanation_en: Anna says 'Just milk, please. No sugar.' This means she wants only milk in her coffee.
explanation.explanation_vi: Anna nói 'Just milk, please. No sugar.' Điều này có nghĩa là cô ấy chỉ muốn sữa trong cà phê, không thêm đường.

examples.note: A typical A1 self-introduction. Key words to catch: 'name', 'Anna', 'Australia'. The contraction 'I'm' sounds like /aɪm/ and means 'I am'.
examples.text: Hello! My name is Anna. I'm from Australia.

examples.note: Listening for time expressions. 'Half past nine' = 9:30. Learners should recognize spoken time phrases, which often differ from written forms.
examples.text: The train leaves at half past nine.

body.objective: Understand and apply basic listening comprehension strategies for short, simple spoken English at CEFR A1 level, including catching key words, numbers, names, and common greetings in slow, clear speech.

explanation.en: At A1 level, listening comprehension focuses on understanding very short, simple spoken texts delivered slowly and clearly: greetings, personal introductions, numbers, prices, times, and simple instructions. Key strategies include: (1) listening for key words (nouns, numbers, names) rather than every word; (2) using context clues to predict what you will hear; (3) recognizing common sound patterns such as contractions ('I'm', 'don't', 'what's') and weak forms; (4) identifying question words (what, where, when, how much) to understand what information is being asked for. Learners should practice listening twice: first for the general idea (gist), then for specific details. Do not worry about understanding every single word — focus on the information needed to answer simple questions.
explanation.vi: Ở trình độ A1, kỹ năng nghe tập trung vào việc hiểu các đoạn nói ngắn, đơn giản, được đọc chậm và rõ: lời chào, giới thiệu bản thân, số, giá tiền, giờ giấc và hướng dẫn đơn giản. Các chiến lược quan trọng gồm: (1) nghe từ khóa (danh từ, con số, tên riêng) thay vì cố nghe từng từ; (2) dùng ngữ cảnh để đoán trước nội dung sẽ nghe; (3) nhận biết các dạng rút gọn phổ biến như 'I'm', 'don't', 'what's' vì người bản xứ thường nói rút gọn; (4) nhận diện từ để hỏi (what, where, when, how much) để biết người nói đang hỏi thông tin gì. Người học nên nghe hai lần: lần đầu nắm ý chính, lần thứ hai nghe chi tiết cụ thể. Đừng lo nếu không hiểu hết từng từ — chỉ cần tập trung vào thông tin cần thiết để trả lời câu hỏi đơn giản.

common_mistakes.why: At natural speaking speed, it is impossible to process every word. Focusing on key words (nouns, numbers, names) and the overall context helps learners capture the main message without getting lost.
common_mistakes.right: Listen for key words and the general idea first, then listen again for specific details.
common_mistakes.wrong: Trying to translate and understand every single word while listening, and missing the rest of the message.

common_mistakes.why: Contractions are extremely common in spoken English and sound different from their written forms. Recognizing them is essential for basic listening comprehension.
common_mistakes.right: Learn common contractions and their full forms: 'don't' = 'do not', 'I'm' = 'I am', 'what's' = 'what is'.
common_mistakes.wrong: Hearing 'don't' as 'don' or 'do not' and being confused by contractions in fast speech.
